scope: Audit of the Maryland routes already covered in this thread for safety, camping, imagery, endpoint reasonableness, and overlap/consolidation.

inventory.galleryPosture: The previous one-image-fits-most assignment was corrected. Exact route-family images remain where supported; other routes use clearly labeled same-river or Maryland tidal/regional context images and do not imply endpoint or current-condition coverage.

accessAudit.disposition: The 61 non-waterbody-confirmed registry entries are named public facility, park, wetland, tidal, or near-water anchors. They remain reasonable planning anchors because route notes require current wetted-edge, carry, parking, hours, tide, and closure verification; no coordinate conflict, suspicious offset, or failure was found for Maryland. The 38 unknown hydrography results are concentrated in tidal or urban/coastal water where the named NHD flowline check is not a sufficient access test.

families.recommendation: Keep the access-pair records. Present the 11 related findings as a selectable corridor ladder; dam boundaries, endpoint camping, gauge relationships, and trip lengths differ.

families.family: Monocacy, Catoctin, Big Pipe, and Little Pipe
families.recommendation: Keep adjacent sections separate where the named access and moving-water corridor differ; use corridor-family navigation rather than deleting the segments.
Keep the shorter and longer endpoint pairs because access, hazards, and shuttle consequences differ.

overlapAndConsolidation.presentationPosture: State browse pages group all reviewed access-ladder records, including planning-only route cards, and retain every route-specific card, endpoint pair, gauge relationship, hazard package, camping posture, and logistics difference. The existing scored-route recommendations remain unchanged.

blockers: Many Maryland tidal and urban endpoints are area or near-water anchors rather than survey-grade wetted-edge coordinates; route notes explicitly require field verification.
No Maryland route has a coordinate-river audit failure or suspicious offset in the current generated report.

validation.routeData: Passed current global route audit for 1166 routes and route typecheck.

validation.access: Generated registry has 228 Maryland entries, all coordinate-consistent and conflict-free.

nextReview: Reopen only when a route owner publishes a more precise wetted-edge coordinate, a route-specific image is rights-cleared, or a new access pair creates a materially distinct corridor rather than another endpoint variant.
